notes.meaning: Christian wives are told to respect and follow the leadership of their husbands. If a husband does not believe the gospel, his wife can help win him to faith through her godly life rather than constant lecturing. When he observes her pure conduct and reverent attitude toward God, he sees the living truth of Christ.

A woman's true beauty should not depend on fancy hairstyles, gold jewelry, or expensive clothes. Real beauty comes from within, showing itself in a gentle and peaceful heart that trusts God. This inward grace does not fade with old age and is of great worth in God's eyes.

Godly women of the Old Testament showed this inner beauty by placing their hope in God and respecting their husbands. Sarah is a prime example, showing Abraham honor and obeying him as head of the family. Believing women are her spiritual daughters today when they do what is right and refuse to give in to fear.

Husbands must live with their wives in a considerate and caring way, recognizing that women are usually physically gentler and need protection. Husbands are called to honor their wives as equal partners who receive the same free gift of eternal life from God. Failing to treat a wife with love damages a husband's fellowship with God and blocks his prayers.

Peter calls all believers to live together in harmony and to share in each other's joys and sorrows. Christians are to love one another like brothers and sisters, showing genuine tenderness and humble minds in every relationship.

Believers must never pay back harm for harm or shout insults at those who insult them. Instead, they must answer hostility with words of blessing and prayer for God's kindness on their enemies. God called His people to act this way so that they may inherit His promised blessing.

Peter quotes Psalm 34 to show that anyone who desires a good and peaceful life must stop speaking evil or telling lies. A person must turn completely away from wrong deeds, actively do good, and chase after peace with others. The Lord watches over the righteous with favor and hears their prayers, but He sets His face against those who do evil.

In normal circumstances, few people seek to hurt someone who is eagerly devoted to doing good. Living an honest, kind, and upright life usually protects a person from unnecessary conflict. Christians can move forward confidently knowing that God watches over their path.

Even when doing what is right results in suffering, God counts believers blessed. Christians should not dread the threats of their persecutors or be shaken by panic. Looking to God keeps the heart steady in the face of human opposition.

Believers are to set Christ apart as the supreme Lord of their hearts rather than living in fear of human threats. Whenever anyone asks about the confident hope they have, Christians must always be ready with a clear explanation of their faith. That defense must never be angry or proud, but delivered with gentleness and deep reverence toward God.

Believers must keep a clear conscience by making sure their everyday behavior honors God. When critics tell lies about them, the steady, godly lives of Christians will prove the charges false and put the slanderers to shame. A clean conscience gives boldness when facing false accusations.

If God's plan includes trials for His people, it is far better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil. Suffering for doing what is right aligns a believer with God's will and brings no guilt. Suffering for one's own sins brings only misery and disgrace.

Christ provides the supreme pattern for innocent suffering because He died once for all to pay for human sins. As the perfectly righteous One, He took the place of unrighteous sinners to bring us into direct fellowship with God. His physical body was put to death on the cross, but He was raised to life by the power of the Spirit.

In the Spirit, Christ went and proclaimed a message to the spirits now held in prison. Many commentators understand this as Christ preaching through Noah to the rebellious generation before the flood, whose souls are now kept imprisoned awaiting final judgment.

differ.view: Lutherans teach that after being made alive, Christ descended into hell in His whole person to proclaim His victory over Satan and the powers of darkness.
Reformed teachers hold that Christ did not literally visit hell, but preached by His Holy Spirit through Noah to the wicked people of that ancient time who are now spirits in prison.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Church teaches that Christ's soul went to the realm of the dead to bring the good news of salvation to the holy souls waiting there and lead them into heaven.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars understand the spirits in prison as fallen angels who rebelled in the days of Noah, to whom the risen Christ announced His triumph.

notes.meaning: These imprisoned spirits refused to listen when God waited patiently for one hundred and twenty years while Noah built the ark. The people ignored every warning until the flood arrived and swept them away. In the end, only eight people—Noah and his family—entered the wooden ark and were brought safely through the floodwaters.

differ.view: Christ, alive after His death, went down to hell to announce His victory over death and the devil, and this verse is the clearest teaching of it.
Christ announced His victory to fallen angels imprisoned for the sins of Noah's time (compare 2 Peter 2:4-5 and Jude 6).

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ's soul went to the realm of the dead as Savior. He brought the good news to the righteous who were waiting there and set them free. He did not free the lost.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars have guessed that an early copyist accidentally dropped a name, so that the verse first said Enoch preached to these spirits. No manuscript supports this.

notes.meaning: The waters of the flood were a picture pointing ahead to baptism, which now symbolizes salvation for believers through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Baptism is not just washing physical dirt off the skin. It is an appeal to God for a clean conscience, made by someone trusting in the living Savior.

differ.view: Baptists teach that water baptism does not save or give new birth in itself, but is an outward sign and pledge of faith in Christ, showing what Jesus already did inside the heart.
Lutherans teach that baptism truly gives salvation and forgiveness of sins as a means of grace, combining water with God's Word and promise.
Reformed churches teach that the outward ceremony of baptism does not save automatically, but is a sign and seal of the inward cleansing of the Holy Spirit received through faith.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Church teaches that baptism is a sacrament that actually washes away sins, brings spiritual rebirth, and unites the believer to the church.

notes.meaning: Jesus has ascended into heaven and now reigns in the place of highest honor at the right hand of God. Every angel, authority, and spiritual power has been placed completely under His command. Because their Savior holds supreme power over all things, suffering Christians have no reason to live in fear.
